Energy Secretary Acts to Protect Mid-Atlantic Grid

Secretary Wright issues emergency order to stabilize the mid-Atlantic grid and minimize the risk of energy shortfalls in 13 states and the District of Columbia.

Energy.gov

November 18, 2026

Estimated Read Time 

 min

WASHINGTON—
U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright 
issued
 an emergency order to reduce the risk of power outages and strengthen grid reliability across the mid-Atlantic region. The order permits PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM), in coordination with Talen Energy Corporation, to run Unit 4 at the Wagner Generating Station in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, to meet anticipated electricity demand. The order follows an application from PJM submitted on October 23, 2026. 
“Energy shortfalls for 65 million Americans are simply unacceptable,” said 
U.S.

Secretary of Energy Chris Wright
.  “Previous orders in the mid-Atlantic region have helped keep the lights on and I’m confident this order will help do so in the coming months as well. Today’s order helps temporarily address the urgent need to strengthen grid reliability and ensure Americans across the mid-Atlantic region have access to affordable, reliable, and secure power, regardless of whether the sun shines or the wind blows.”  
Secretary Wright previously 
granted
 PJM’s requests to operate Wagner Unit 4 beyond its operating limit to help maintain grid reliability. 
PJM relied on Wagner Unit 4 during periods of unusually high temperatures earlier this summer, using the unit’s remaining operating hours. PJM has since reaffirmed to the Department of Energy (DOE) the continued need for Wagner Unit 4 to meet high electricity demand, strengthen grid reliability, and reduce the risk of power outages across the mid-Atlantic region.  
The renewed order is effective from November 18, 2026, through December 31, 2026.
